findings.reason: The protected SQL solution calculates monthly working percentages of active drivers for 2020 using a WITH RECURSIVE Months CTE (1 to 12). For each month, correlated subqueries calculate distinct working drivers (from AcceptedRides JOIN Rides) and active drivers (Drivers with join_date before the start of next month). It handles zero active drivers via IFNULL/NULLIF and rounds percentages to 2 decimal places. The query runs in O(d + r + a) time and O(a) space; no candidate is required.
Correlated distinct driver count over monthly ride requested_at date ranges divided by cumulative active driver count up to month-end accurately produces percentage for each 2020 month.

Fixed 12-month spine evaluates 12 constant subquery pairs over d drivers, r rides, and a accepted rides in O(d + r + a) total time and O(a) space for distinct driver hash sets. Complexity evidence is bounded-domain certified and hash-bound.
Accepts Drivers, Rides, and AcceptedRides tables, returning 12 rows with columns month and working_percentage.

The approach accurately details 12-month recursive CTE generation, correlated distinct working driver counts, month-end cumulative active driver counts, NULLIF/IFNULL zero division handling, and O(d + r + a) time / O(a) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover accepted ride row counting traps, all-driver denominator inaccuracies, ride-only month grouping omission risk, pre-2020 driver join eligibility, month-end join date boundaries, rejected request exclusion, non-2020 ride exclusions, and zero active driver safety.

App SQL and native SQL solutions both execute the identical 12-month recursive CTE with correlated active/working driver queries with SHA-256 digests dae9e7514873f539f48be2065ea85d0960fb96dd7eea3a5f35891b01ef330b6d and d5e191bc3803fa70ae885582ad734362329054a726b6590af6f6e6f9962d9048.
